ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $M$ is a point on side $BC$. Connect $AM$ and draw $DE \perp AM$ with $E$ as the foot of the perpendicular. If $DE=DC=1$ and $AE=2EM$, what is the length of $BM$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since rectangle ABCD, with DE$\perp$AM, \\
it follows that $\angle$C=$\angle$AED=$\angle$B=$90^\circ$, with AB=DE=CD=1, and AD$\parallel$BC,\\
hence, $\angle$DAE=$\angle$AEM. In $\triangle$ADE and $\triangle$MAB
\[ \left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle B=\angle AED\\
\angle DAE=\angle AMB\\
DE=AB
\end{array}\right. \]
it follows that $\triangle$ADE$\cong$$\triangle$MAB (by AAS),\\
thus, AE=BM=2EM;\\
In the right triangle ABM, AB$^{2}$+BM$^{2}$=AM$^{2}$, that is, 1$^{2}$+($2EM$)$^{2}$=($3EM$)$^{2}$,\\
Solving for this yields: $EM=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}$,\\
therefore, BM=\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}}.
